text:
### Observed differences

- In the earlier window, the six activities A28, A30, A31, A32, A33 and A34 each ran in every trace (200 of 200), sitting between A25 (mean relative position about 0.62) and A26 (about 0.83); in the later window the first group runs in about 46 in 100 traces and the second in about 56 in 100. [OCC019, OCC020, OCC021, OCC022, OCC023, OCC024, POS001, POS002]
- Earlier, the two groups were always executed together and in sequence: A25 preceded A28/A30/A31 in 100 in 100 traces, these preceded A32/A33/A34 in 100 in 100, and A32/A33/A34 preceded A26 in 100 in 100, with no fixed order inside each group. In the later window the two groups share a trace in only about 2 in 100 cases: about 45 in 100 later traces contain only the first group, about 54 in 100 only the second, and essentially none contain neither. [REL001, REL004, REL007, REL010, REL013, REL015, REL018, REL019, REL022, REL025]
- The bypass shows directly in the transition profiles: A25 now leads straight to A32, A33 and A34 (about 16–20 in 100 of its outgoing transitions each, previously unobserved), and A28, A30 and A31 now lead straight to A26 (about 26–35 in 100 each, previously unobserved), while their transitions into the other group have nearly vanished. [DIR016, DIR018, DIR020, DIR021]
- Accordingly, the positional gap from A25 to A32/A33/A34 and from A28/A30/A31 to A26 shrank from 4–5 steps to 1–3 steps, A25's mean position moved later (about 0.62 to 0.67) and A26's moved earlier (about 0.83 to 0.81), as expected when traces shorten by a skipped group. [LAG004, LAG005, LAG006, LAG007, LAG013, LAG019, POS001, POS002]
- Away from this segment the differences are modest: a flipped majority branch among A20, A27, A29 and A21, participation shifts of about 6–8 in 100 traces for A16–A19, somewhat more repetition of A38 and somewhat more frequent A39. [DIR014, OCC015, OCC017, OCC027, OCC028]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the hypothesis that the segment between A25 and A26 changed from a mandatory two-block sequence into a choice between the blocks: A28, A30 and A31 (always executed together) and A32, A33 and A34 (always executed together) ran one after the other in every earlier trace, whereas in the later window about 45 in 100 traces execute only the first block, about 54 in 100 only the second, and about 2 in 100 both — so one block is now skipped in nearly every trace, while A25 and A26 still occur in every trace and keep their order around the segment. The change is shown directly and consistently: participation fell from 100% to about 47% (93 of 200 traces) and about 56% (111 of 200), between-block co-occurrence collapsed from 100% to about 2%, new direct transitions A25→A32/A33/A34 and A28/A30/A31→A26 appeared, and the position gaps compressed from 4–5 to 1–3 steps; each of these items exceeds the difference seen in about 199 of 200 random re-splits. [OCC019, OCC022, REL015, REL001, DIR016, DIR018, LAG004, LAG007]

Limitations: the many agreeing items describe one underlying difference rather than independent confirmations; the exact split between the blocks (about 45 vs 54 in 100) and the both-block residue (about 4 of 200 later traces) carry sampling uncertainty; and the evidence cannot rule out that the two windows draw different case mixes — for example coexisting variants sampled in shifted proportions — rather than a modified single process. A few lag items in this segment rest on only about 4 later observations and were not relied upon. [REL015, LAG010, LAG016]

Other differences:
- In a separate region, the majority branch on the edges A20→A27/A29, A27→A21/A29 and A29→A21/A27 flipped from about 55:45 to about 46:54, with all four activities present in every trace in both windows. [DIR014, DIR017, DIR019]
- A16–A19 shifted modestly in how often they run (A16 and A18 down about 6–8 in 100 traces, A17 and A19 up about 6–8 in 100), A24's outgoing shares moved toward A17 and A19, and A18 and A19 route to A25 in opposite directions. [OCC015, OCC016, OCC017, OCC018, DIR015, DIR012, DIR013]
- A38 occurred somewhat more often per trace (mean about 1.55 to 1.70) and A39 became somewhat more frequent (participation about 63 to 68 in 100; mean about 0.79 to 0.94), with A38 routing slightly more to A39. [OCC027, OCC028, DIR027, DIR028, DIR029]
- Remaining occurrence differences (A01–A13, A35, A36, A40, A41) are small — at most about 7 in 100 — and consistent with sampling variation between two 200-trace windows. [OCC001, OCC009, OCC011, OCC012, OCC025, OCC029]
